sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Findlay, Ohio?
sections.html:
Findlay is a mid-sized, employer-anchored market: the city is the Hancock County seat, the second-largest city in Northwest Ohio, and sits about 40 miles south of Toledo. Houses here sell to people who work at the big local plants and offices, so timing often follows hiring and plant schedules more than the calendar.

Laid out along the Blanchard River, which runs east to west through town, Findlay grew from Fort Findlay, a stockade built during the War of 1812. The first town lots were platted in 1821. An oil and gas boom in the 1880s pushed the population from 4,633 in 1880 to 18,553 in 1890, and many of the older neighborhoods near downtown still carry housing from that era. Newer subdivisions sit toward the edges of the city's roughly 19.6 square miles of land.

A seller here usually weighs three routes: a listing with an agent, a sale without one, or a direct purchase by an investor or cash buyer. The sections below cover the local facts that change the math on each route.

sections.h2: Who lives in Findlay and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Findlay is a smaller, lower-priced market than the Columbus and Cleveland suburbs, and the Census Bureau figures below show it. Owner-occupied homes make up just under 60 percent of housing, so renters are a real share of the buyer and landlord pool.

The 2010 Census counted 41,202 people, so the city has held roughly steady for fifteen years. A short average commute of 16.1 minutes is a selling point for buyers who work at the plants, the hospital or the university.

sections.h2: How does the Blanchard River affect selling a Findlay house?
sections.html:
Flood risk is the biggest property-specific question in Findlay, and buyers and lenders will ask about it. The Blanchard River crested at 18.46 feet in the 2007 flood, which caused around $100 million in damage and came close to the 1913 flood.

The city's floodplain page sets the rules a seller should know:

  • Findlay takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, so any property in the city can carry a flood policy through the program or a private carrier.
  • Any activity inside a Special Flood Hazard Area, including grading, new construction and changes to existing structures, needs a Flood Development Permit before work starts.
  • Damage to a structure in that area, whether from flood, fire or wind, must be reported to the Zoning Department so a damage assessment can be made.
  • Parcels can be checked against the flood zone through the Hancock County Auditor maps, and the Zoning Department will help.

The city has also submitted a Letter of Map Revision to FEMA after the first phase of river benching, proposing that significant land come out of or shrink within the mapped flood zones, and the city keeps a list of the affected parcels on its flood information page. Whether your lot is on that list is worth checking before you set a price, since a map change can alter what a buyer pays for insurance.

Weather also works on the house itself. Findlay averages about 37.7 inches of precipitation and 23.8 inches of snow a year, with record lows near minus 21 degrees, so buyers look hard at roofs, gutters, sump pumps and basements.

sections.h2: Which Findlay employers and roads bring in buyers?
sections.html:
Findlay's job base is unusually concentrated, which helps house demand. Marathon Petroleum is headquartered downtown, Whirlpool runs what is considered the largest dishwasher plant in the world by production, and distribution centers for Lowe's, Kohl's, Best Buy and Campbell Soup operate in and around the city. Cooper Tire, founded in Findlay in 1914, was acquired by Goodyear in 2021.

The city's 2024 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, lists these top employers:

  • Blanchard Valley Regional Health Center: 3,165 employees
  • Marathon Petroleum: 2,159
  • Whirlpool: 1,930
  • Goodyear: 895
  • Findlay City Schools: 865
  • The University of Findlay: 548

Interstate 75 passes through town, and US 68 ends at its northern terminus here. US 224 and Ohio routes 12, 15, 37 and 568 also run through the city. Students come from the University of Findlay, which enrolls more than 4,100, and Owens Community College. The public schools belong to the Findlay City School District, and Findlay High School serves grades 9 to 12.

sections.h2: What does the Hancock County Auditor charge to transfer a Findlay deed?
sections.html:
Hancock County charges a conveyance fee of $3 per thousand dollars conveyed, rounded to the nearest ten cents, plus a $0.50 transfer fee for each parcel. Checks go to the Hancock County Auditor, and certain transfers are exempt from the conveyance fee.

Per the county's property transfer page, every transfer needs a DTE 100 conveyance form (or a DTE 100(EX) exemption form) and a notarized deed with an accurate legal description. The Real Estate Division sits in room 21 on the second floor of the Hancock County Courthouse, 300 S. Main Street, Findlay, and can be reached at 419-424-7015.

Recording is a separate step at the recorder. Since January 2025 the county charges $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each added page, under its fee schedule. Ohio law also says the deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or another listed officer (ORC 5301.01).

sections.h2: What must a Findlay seller disclose to a buyer?
sections.html:
An Ohio seller of a one-to-four unit home must complete the state Residential Property Disclosure form and hand a signed copy to each buyer as soon as practicable (ORC 5302.30). If the buyer gets the form after signing the contract, the buyer has three business days to rescind.

The statute lists exemptions that matter in a city with older family homes. They include transfers by an executor or other fiduciary, transfers to a spouse or a lineal relative, and transfers by an heir who inherited the property and did not live in it during the prior year. Even when the form is not required, the law still bars concealing a known defect.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Findlay house quickly?
sections.html:
The fastest path is a buyer who does not need a mortgage or an appraisal, but a traditional listing can still work in Findlay when the house shows well and the price matches the neighborhood.

  • List with an agent: widest buyer pool, with repairs, showings and the lender timeline all on you.
  • Sell by owner: saves a commission but you handle the disclosure form, the DTE 100 and the deed yourself.
  • Sell to a cash buyer: sells as-is and can close on your schedule, usually at a discount to a repaired listing.
  • Sell to a neighbor or relative: simpler paperwork, though the disclosure and conveyance forms still apply unless an exemption fits.

A flood-zone parcel, a landlord with tenants in place, or a house needing a roof can tilt the choice toward an as-is sale. Get at least two written offers and compare net proceeds after the conveyance fee, the unpaid property tax and any payoff.

faqs.q: Is Findlay a good place to sell a house right now?
faqs.a: Findlay is a steady market tied to large employers rather than a boom town. The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied home value at $191,000 and shows the population roughly flat since 2010, so pricing close to nearby sales matters more than waiting for a spike.

faqs.q: Does a Findlay house in the flood zone sell for less?
faqs.a: It can, because flood insurance is a cost the buyer takes on. Check your parcel on the Hancock County Auditor maps, ask the city Zoning Department about any proposed map revision, and gather any elevation or flood insurance records before listing.

faqs.q: How much does Hancock County charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The county conveyance fee is $3 per thousand dollars conveyed plus $0.50 per parcel, and recording costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each added page. Exempt transfers use the DTE 100(EX) form, and the Auditor's Real Estate Division can confirm the exact total.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Findlay house before selling?
faqs.a: No Ohio rule requires repairs before a sale, but you must disclose known defects on the state form if the sale is covered. Buyers who use a mortgage often ask for repairs after inspection, while an as-is buyer prices the work in.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a Findlay sale?
faqs.a: Deeds for property in Findlay are recorded with the Hancock County Recorder in Findlay, after the County Auditor stamps the conveyance. Ohio law treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later buyer who had no knowledge of it (ORC 5301.25), so title companies file promptly.
